blockdesc-foodbowl-fired-*: Put raw or cooked meat in it: kept dogs walk to it and eat. Livestock leaves it alone.

itemdesc-groomingbrush: Hold right click on a dirty animal to brush it clean. Cleans twice as well as a wisp of dry grass, and faster. Wears out with use.
itemdesc-chickencoop-*: Right-click the ground to build a small raised coop there, stretching away from you: on four posts, with a pitched roof, a little ramp up to the pop hole, two hen boxes inside and steps up to a gate at the back, where you can walk in to collect the eggs. Room for 6 to 8 hens, and shelter underneath too. Needs a clear spot of 5 by 9 blocks, 6 high.
coop-onground: Right-click the top of the ground to build the coop
coop-noroom: Not enough room for the coop: it needs a clear spot of 5 by 9 blocks, 6 high
coop-noground: The posts and the ramp of the coop need solid ground under them
coop-blocked: Something is standing where a part of the coop would go
blockdesc-waterer-raw: Fire it in a pit kiln to make a waterer.
blockdesc-waterer-fired: A clay bell drinker: a wide, low dish that even chickens can reach. Fill it with a bucket; thirsty animals walk to it and drink.

handbook-guide-title: Livestock Welfare: caring for your animals
handbook-guide-text:
Livestock Welfare
Happy animals, healthy herd.

Your sheep, goats, pigs and chickens have needs of their own. Look at an animal to see how it is doing, or sneak + right click it with an empty hand for a full report in chat.

Water
Animals get thirsty, faster when it is hot. They walk to ponds, rivers and puddles within 16 blocks and drink there. You can also give them water in a barrel, a placed bucket or a clay waterer, but they really drink those empty, so refill them.

Shelter
Rain, snow, cold and strong sun stress animals in the open. Build them a roof within 24 blocks with an open way in: in bad weather and at night they go under it, and they sleep there until morning. A closed barn also keeps out the cold. Petting (right click with an empty hand) calms a stressed animal.

Cleanliness
Crowded pens, muck and rot make animals filthy, and filthy animals can fall sick and infect others. Shovel up the muck (it gives rot for compost) and groom your animals with dry grass or a grooming brush. Chickens can't be groomed: give them dry sand for dust baths.

Babies and orphans
Lambs, kids and piglets suckle from their mother, so keep her healthy. An orphan doesn't know the trough yet: sneak and hold right click with milk or food to feed it from your hand.

Old age
Every animal has its own lifespan. Old animals no longer breed, and one that dies of old age gives fewer drops, so cull them in time.

Chickens
Hold grain and your hens follow you. The chicken coop kit builds a raised coop with two hen boxes.

Every system can be tuned or switched off in ModConfig/livestockwelfare.json.
tip-first-animal: Livestock Welfare: your animals now need water, shelter and care. Sneak + right click an animal with an empty hand for its full status, and read the "Livestock Welfare" page in the handbook (H) to learn more.
